children: Altimeter Capital
CEO
Brad Gerstner
dismissed warnings that artificial intelligence (AI) could threaten human survival on Friday, calling the rhetoric overblown after a former
Anthropic
researcher’s exit stirred fresh debate over AI safety.
AI Safety Debate Continues
“What I didn’t like this week is these hyperbolic scare tactics, which I think are hiding behind a political agenda,” Gerstner told CNBC’s “Halftime Report.”

Gerstner said AI firms have taken precautions compared with earlier tech booms. “We ignored all of the extraordinary steps already being taken, unlike in the age of the internet, unlike with social media, to get ahead of these downsides,” he said. Altimeter holds stakes in Anthropic,
OpenAI
and enterprise AI vendors
Glean
and
Databricks Inc.
, which focus on data and large-scale language systems.
His remarks followed a viral post. Former Anthropic researcher
Jacob Coxon
quit this week, accusing AI companies on X of “
” in the pursuit of superintelligence. The comments added to an already
over the buildout of massive AI data centers.
Delangue Downplays Coxon’s Authority on AI Risk
In an X post on Friday,
Hugging Face
‘s CEO
Clement Delangue
also questioned the outsized attention on Coxon’s warning. He wrote on X, “Sorry, but asking Jacob about AI extinction risk is like asking your AC guy about climate change.”
Sorry, but asking Jacob about AI extinction risk is like asking your AC guy about climate change.
Not saying it's necessarily uninteresting or wrong per se but let’s keep things in perspective and hear from the full range of expertise across the ecosystem!

children: In an earlier post, Delangue responded to Anthropic’s
Evan Hubinger

, who estimated that there was a 10% chance AI could cause human extinction within the next decade. Delangue argued, “If they truly believe the risk is that high… then we need 100x more research and understanding of it. That requires them to openly share their models, datasets, training code, and agent traces.”

If they truly believe the risk is that high, and I think they do, then we need 100x more research and understanding of it. That requires them to openly share their models, datasets, training code, and agent traces.
Former OpenAI Researcher Warns of Autonomous Risk
Not everyone agrees the alarm is misplaced.
Daniel Kokotajlo

, former OpenAI governance researcher and executive director of the AI Futures Project, told CNBC’s “Squawk on the Street” that model advances are trending in “a very concerning direction.” He said, “It seems like a year from now, two years from now, three years from now, they really will be able to have AIs that can do the entire research process themselves, that will be autonomously self-improving, and that could go very badly.”
